definitions.gloss: long-cherished wish; longtime ambition; heartfelt desire
definitions.explanation: A wish or goal that one has held for a very long time, often implying years of effort or patience toward its fulfillment.

examples.japanese: {宿願|しゅくがん}を{果|は}たす。
{宿願|しゅくがん}だったオリンピック{出場|しゅつじょう}がついに{実現|じつげん}した。
examples.english: My long-held dream of competing in the Olympics finally came true.

examples.japanese: {三十年|さんじゅうねん}にわたる{宿願|しゅくがん}であった{和平|わへい}{条約|じょうやく}の{締結|ていけつ}が{達成|たっせい}された。
examples.english: The signing of the peace treaty, a goal pursued for thirty years, was achieved.

notes:
A compound of {宿|しゅく} (long-standing) and {願|がん} (wish/prayer). A literary, elevated word that emphasizes the depth and duration of a desire. Often used in formal speeches, news articles, and historical writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {宿願|しゅくがん}を{果|は}たす: to fulfill a long-cherished wish
- {宿願|しゅくがん}が{叶|かな}う: a long-held wish comes true
- {宿願|しゅくがん}を{達成|たっせい}する: to achieve a long-held goal
- {宿願|しゅくがん}の{実現|じつげん}: realization of a long-cherished wish

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {悲願|ひがん}: earnest wish — similar formality but adds a nuance of desperate longing or repeated failed attempts
- {念願|ねんがん}: long-cherished desire — very close in meaning; slightly more common in everyday usage
- {願望|がんぼう}: desire, aspiration — more general and less literary
